messages:
raj: Heads up — seeing a burst of NVIDIA Xid 13 (CE failure / GPU page fault) on p4d-uswest2 pool since 14:02 UTC
raj: avg ~12/min, affects ~8 pins across 3 hosts, all during long decode jobs (>8k token windows) using batch_size=32
raj: nvml shows ECC errors incrementing on GPU 2/5 on host ip-10-0-23-7
olivia: thanks, can you paste dmesg / kernel log snippet?
raj: snippet pasted:
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:18:00): 13, pid=12345, mod=ucc, reason=0x49c
raj: also a quick extract from nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.mode.current,xecc.corrected,xecc.uncorrected --format=csv,noheader:
GPU-2, On, 124, 2
raj: numbers look like correctable ECCs accumulating then 1-2 uncorrectables
marta: short take — Xid13 often surfaces for ECC-corrected overflow when sustained high memory pressure + older driver, or intermittent hardware/thermal issues
marta: check driver 525 vs 550 and whether copy engine errors coincide with these timestamps
sean: recall we saw a similar pattern last quarter: long kv-cache + continuous batching triggered a single GPU to leak host pinned memory and eventually Xid13 after ~2-3 hours of steady decode
raj: driver on affected hosts: 525.85.12, kernel 5.15.0-1011-gcp
olivia: temporary mitigation: reduce batch_size to 8 or cap context to 4k for these pools, and throttle continuous streams to avoid steady-state memory growth
olivia: schedule drain of 3 affected GPUs for overnight maintenance (replace thermal pads / reseat) :wrench:
raj: created drain task infra/drains/179250 — cordon + migrate pods, ETA 03:00 UTC
infra-bot: host ip-10-0-23-7 cordon initiated by raj
marta: telemetry note: we should correlate Xid13 events with workload fields: model name, decoding strategy (topk/top-p), tokens/sec, kv-cache bytes, quantization (int8/4bit), and batching window length
marta: quick heuristic mapping (for our triage runbook):
- Xid 13 -> sustained memory pressure, ECC correctables then uncorrectables, often long-context decodes or memory leak in runtime
- Xid 31 -> illegal memory access, often buggy kernels or driver/kernel mismatch or bad CUDA kernels (nvfuser edge cases)
- Xid 48 -> likely thermal / power droop or pci bus errors (check fans, power rails)
- Xid 79 -> firmware/PCIe/CPU bus errors, sometimes correlated with bad cabling or host BIOS
sean: add note: MIG can change visible Xid behaviour; also different driver versions map same hardware failure to different Xid codes — always capture driver+firmware+bios in event metadata
raj: will run a controlled repro: long_decode_runner --model z-13b --ctx 8192 --bs 16 --duration 3h --track-kv --emit-nvml
olivia: pls also pull nvidia-smi dmon and nv-hostengine logs during repro
marta: also enable a short-lived aggressive collector: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,utilization.gpu,mem.used,fan.speed --format=csv -l 1 > /tmp/gpu-trace.csv
sean: we should add an automated alert to bump host to "degraded" state on first uncorrectable ECC > 0, with 4h auto-retry before auto-replace
raj: for follow-up, add to Redwood Optimize recommendations: if Xid13 frequency exceeds threshold, recommend smaller batch sizes, aggressive KV cache trimming, or model quantization fallback to reduce memory working set
olivia: cooling logs look suspicious on host-7 — fan rpm dropped to 20% for ~30s at 13:55 UTC, coincident with first Xid spike
marta: ok. immediate plan: 1) drain 3 GPUs overnight, 2) collect repro traces on a spare host, 3) tag affected GPUs for hardware inspection/reseat, 4) add telemetry correlation fields and degraded-host automation
raj: noted. I'll post drain progress and attach collected logs here after the run
olivia: thanks — if replacement needed, coordinate with vendors channel and mark capacity for dedicated tenants
sean: thanks team. this mapping should go into the eng-infra triage playbook (short doc) so oncall can run quick heuristics
raj: will draft playbook snippet and link it to incidents page
olivia: keep updates here :thumbsup:
